question: In rhegmatogenous retinal detachment, the central vision is typically preserved until the detachment reaches and involves the macula.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is true. The macula sits in the posterior pole away from the detachment that starts peripherally. Central vision is preserved in 'macula-on' detachments. This distinction determines surgical urgency: macula-on = operate the same day; macula-off = still urgent but not same-day emergency.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. This is why the macular status is the single most important prognostic factor in retinal detachment. 'Macula-on' detachment (central vision preserved) is a surgical emergency requiring same-day repair; 'macula-off' detachment carries a permanently worse visual prognosis even after successful reattachment.
